title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows and optimize cache hygiene
author: Priya Malhotra
release_notes: Improve CI latency and stability by splitting workflows, reducing redundant steps, and improving cache keys. No user-facing changes.
description: Motivation: Our monolithic CI workflow had grown slow and brittle - lint, tests, and release automation ran in a single large workflow which increased queue time, made cache invalidation hard to reason about, and amplified flakiness. This PR splits the workflows into three focused pipelines (lint, test, release) and standardizes cache keys, pinning of GH Actions and node images, and shared job templates to reduce duplication. Changes: - Split .github/workflows/ci.yml into .github/workflows/lint.yml, .github/workflows/test.yml, and .github/workflows/release.yml. - Introduced workflow templates in .github/workflow-templates/ci-job-template.yml for consistent setup/checkout/caching steps. - Standardized cache key format: repo-{{ matrix.os }}-node-{{ matrix.node-version }}-deps-{{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}. - Pinned widely-used actions to specific vX.Y.Z to avoid unexpected breaking changes. - Reduced matrix sizes for individual workflows (split lint to run on ubuntu-latest only) while keeping full matrix for integration tests. - Added an optional fast-path for PRs touching docs or markdown only (skips tests if only content changes). Commits: ["a1b2c3d: split workflows and add templates", "d4e5f6a: standardize cache keys and pin actions", "f7g8h9i: add docs-only fast-path and update runbook"] Changed areas / files (high-level): [".github/workflows/lint.yml", ".github/workflows/test.yml", ".github/workflows/release.yml", ".github/workflow-templates/ci-job-template.yml", ".github/actions/cache-utils/*", "package.json (ci scripts)", "docs/ci.md"] Review summary: - Diego: Asked to justify cache key based on package-lock.json hash and suggested adding fallback when lockfile is missing. Response: added fallback to use yarn.lock or package.json timestamp. - Elena: Asked for a phased rollout and short-circuit for small PRs to avoid extra CI cost; suggested feature flag via labels. Response: implemented docs-only fast-path and added an opt-out label `ci/full-run`. - Samir: Noted potential flakiness in integration tests; requested a canary pipeline. Response: added nightly canary and moved the most flaky tests to a separate job with larger retry/backoff. CI checks: ["lint: passed (ubuntu-latest)", "unit-tests: passed with 1 flaky test retried", "integration-tests: passed (canary rerun)", "release: dry-run success", "workflow-lint: passed"] Notable CI events: initial run failed due to an action pin resolving to a pre-release; pinned to a specific release fixed the issue. One flaky integration test (tests/streaming/test_retry.py) required an extra retry step in the job. Rollout plan: - Rollout to main immediately after merge. - Monitor CI duration and cache hit rates in the next 72 hours (Dashboard: Infra > CI > Cache hygiene). - If cache hit rate drops below 60% revert cache key change and investigate. Merge: Squash-merged by "Diego Ramirez" on 2026-02-20. Follow-ups: - ENG-4278: add CI analytics export to track cache hits per repo. - ENG-4302: evaluate further matrix pruning for cost optimization. Why this is safe: no production code changed; only CI infra and docs. The fast-path respects explicit opt-out label to avoid accidental skips on important PRs.
